quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: If you see animals near the road while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and drive carefully.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: Slow down and drive carefully if you see animals near the road. Animals may suddenly run or change direction. Some animals travel in groups, so more animals may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: How should you check for vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Look in the inside rearview mirror.
Look in the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly and safely to get back into your lane sooner. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Wear both parts of a two-part seat belt. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. Even if you have an automatic shoulder belt, you must also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: What does California's Move Over law require?

options.text: All vehicles must stay in the right lane at all times.
Trucks must use the left lane.
All vehicles must leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles must leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights on.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with its lights on is stopped on the side of the road, you must move away from that lane if you can do so safely. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and drive carefully. This law also applies to stopped tow trucks and Department of Transportation vehicles.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring at the road directly ahead of you.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: To stay aware of hazards, scan the road and check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds. Do not stare at just the road ahead. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beam.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. It is unsafe and illegal to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other cars on a two-lane road and pass them repeatedly, what will happen?

options.text: You will reach your destination much faster and more safely.
You will increase your chances of a collision.
You will help prevent traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will increase your chances of a collision.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Each time you pass a vehicle, your risk of a collision increases.

questions.question: To avoid sudden maneuvers, how far ahead should you look while driving?

options.text: About 5 to 10 seconds ahead.
About 10 to 15 seconds ahead.
About 15 to 20 seconds ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: About 10 to 15 seconds ahead.
questions.explanation: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle to avoid sudden moves. This gives you time to see hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: At what speed can hydroplaning occur on wet roads?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when there is standing water on the road. Most tires can channel water away at speeds up to 35 mph. At speeds above 35 mph, tires cannot channel water as well, and your tires may lose contact with the road like water skis.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully.
Come to a complete stop as fast as possible.
Stop and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and drive carefully. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: You are exiting the freeway on a curved ramp going downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: If a traffic signal light is not working, what must you do?

options.text: Stop, then go when it is safe.
Stop and let all other traffic go first.
Slow down or stop only if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: If a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection like all directions have stop signs. Proceed cautiously when it is safe.

questions.question: Why is space around your vehicle important?

options.text: Other drivers can cut in front of you, improving traffic flow.
You have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It protects you from injury in a collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your vehicle so you have time to safely react if another driver makes a mistake. Extra space may give you time to brake or steer away from a vehicle moving into your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle sign with black letters means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of two-way, two-lane roads where you also see line markings that prohibit passing.

questions.question: What happens when you brake hard on ice and snow?

options.text: You stop faster.
The front wheels lock, and you lose steering control.
The brakes stay warm and do not freeze.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front wheels lock, and you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Drive at a safe speed for conditions to avoid excessive braking.

questions.question: You want to pass a bicyclist in a narrow lane while an oncoming vehicle approaches. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and then pass the bicyclist.
Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
Wait until the bicyclist leaves the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
questions.explanation: Handle one danger at a time. Do not try to squeeze between the bicyclist and the other vehicle. Slow down to let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the bicyclist when it is safe.

questions.question: When you are ready to make a right turn, what should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn right away.
Stop and let all other traffic go first.
Slow down or stop if needed, then turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or stop if needed, then turn.
questions.explanation: When turning right, signal about 100 feet before the turn, reduce speed, stop behind the limit line if needed, then make the turn.

questions.question: A truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus can turn.
Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to squeeze your vehicle between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus has finished turning before you turn.

questions.question: A child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Beep your horn.
Assume the child has full control of the bicycle.
Be ready for anything unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable. Young riders often make sudden direction changes without warning. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see, so always expect the unexpected.

questions.question: Many actions are dangerous while driving. Which one is also illegal?

options.text: Listening to music through headphones in both ears.
Adjusting your side mirrors.
Reading a map.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listening to music through headphones in both ears.
questions.explanation: Wearing headphones in both ears while driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You may never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Right, toward the edge of the road.
Left, toward the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels away from the center of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What does California's "Basic Speed Law" require?

options.text: Drive at the same speed as other traffic.
Never drive faster than what is safe for current conditions.
Always drive at the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never drive faster than what is safe for current conditions.
questions.explanation: The "Basic Speed Law" says you must never drive faster than is safe for current conditions. For example, driving 45 mph in a 55 mph zone during heavy fog is illegal because it is unsafe, even though you are below the speed limit.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing them.
Cars coming toward them.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward them.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles that are going straight. You can only turn left when it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which roadway freezes first when wet?

options.text: Bridges and overpasses.
Intersections.
Tunnels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bridges and overpasses.
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other road surfaces do.

questions.question: To turn left from a one-way street onto a one-way street, start from which lane?

options.text: The leftmost lane.
The center lane.
Any lane, if it seems safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leftmost lane.
questions.explanation: Start a left turn from a one-way street in the far left lane. Watch for pedestrians, motorcycles, and bicycles near the curb because they can also legally use the left lane. Turn into any lane that is safely open.

questions.question: You hit an animal with your vehicle on a California highway. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured animal off the road.
Call the humane society or police.
Continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call the humane society or police.
questions.explanation: If you hit an animal, call the California Highway Patrol, the humane society, or police. Do not leave the animal or try to move it yourself.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a residential area if no other speed limit is posted?

options.text: 20 mph.
25 mph.
30 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit in residential and business areas is 25 mph unless a different speed limit is posted.

questions.question: What usually causes a locked wheel skid?

options.text: Braking too hard while driving slowly.
Braking gently while driving slowly.
Braking too hard while driving fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking too hard while driving fast.
questions.explanation: Locked wheel skids happen when a driver brakes too hard while driving at high speed. Use your brakes smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: A round sign means you are approaching railroad tracks. This sign is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When must you use your low beam headlights?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beam light reflects off precipitation and creates glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights to use with low beams.

questions.question: What are the consequences of misusing a disabled parking placard?

options.text: Losing the placard only.
A fine only.
Loss of placard, a fine, and/or jail time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of placard, a fine, and/or jail time.
questions.explanation: Misusing a disabled placard is a crime. Consequences include losing parking privileges, a fine up to $1,000, and up to six months in jail.

questions.question: A driver sees pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk. What should the driver do?

options.text: Continue. The driver has the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the pedestrians have fully crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the divided highway ends ahead. Be ready to change lanes or adjust your position.

questions.question: When can a person legally ride in the back of a pickup truck?

options.text: When the truck bed sides are at least 24 inches high.
When the truck bed is covered with a camper shell.
When sitting in a secured seat and wearing an approved safety belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: When sitting in a secured seat and wearing an approved safety belt.
questions.explanation: Do not allow anyone to ride in the back of a truck unless the vehicle has a seat and the person uses both the seat and a safety belt.
